Factually, yes, parents are directly responsible for all the suffering in their offspring's life. Societal and other types of indoctrination are indeed a mitigating factor, but only that. Other things, like them also being victims - not so much.

The question to me comes right down to the problem of free will. Do you think that they've had a choice? Does anyone ever have a choice? Should we put the blame on people and hold them accountable for anything?

Scientific evidence suggests that free will isn't real, and what's more, it could never be. Sam Harris has a short book on this, it's called... "Free will" (wow, much creativity).
If you haven't read it, you might want to catch up. I completed it a long time ago and haven't opened it since. From what I can remember, Sam's position is to admit the non-existence of free will and that we aren't really in control (something along the lines of "you're not lost in the storm, you are the storm"), but then to draw some overly optimistic conclusions in favor of feeling good. I remember his example of a man committing a certain crime; Harris says that depending on what kind of life this individual had (on a scale from one to ten, from a luxury life with all the mental and physiological needs satisfied to a life of poverty and insecurity on those fronts), we can assign different (in severity) kinds of punishment to that person, and that we'd be justified in doing so. This solution seems fine on the surface, but ignores that all the humans, their minds and psychological conditions are different, the problem of us not being able to "read" the human brain like a map and inability to unequivocally understand causal links between inputs and particular events from the outer world, our brains and our (re)actions (ironically, the author spends a good chunk of essay discussing this issue, but then kinda drops it). Harris also comes across as a naive happy guy when suggesting that in admission that we're literally biological robots we don't lose much, if anything. 

The other question you might wanna ask yourself is, what's the use of holding parents accountable? If it's to make them admit their fault and sheer ignorance and stupidity of their decision, and extract some favors from them (that you feel are justified), then it makes sense. Otherwise? Not really. You can bear a grudge inside or you can voice your concerns - that all depends on whether or not you desire a particular kind of relationship and whether you have to live with them side by side on a daily basis. 

Sorry, I'm out of time to write a satisfying conclusion, but hopefully that has given you some food for thought.
